passages.text: ECLIPSE, in astronomy, a privation of the light of one of the luminaries, by the interposition of some opaque body.

An eclipse of the sun happens when the moon comes between the sun and the earth; and an eclipse of the moon, when the earth comes between the sun and the moon, so that the shadow of the earth falls upon the moon.
Eclipses of the sun happen only at the new moon, and those of the moon only at the full, and then only when the moon is near one of her nodes.
The times of eclipses are now computed by astronomers with such exactness that they may be foretold many years before they happen.
The Chaldeans found that eclipses return in nearly the same order after a period of about 18 years and 11 days, which is called the Saros.
The vulgar in all ages have looked upon eclipses as omens of some great calamity; but this superstition has been dispelled by the knowledge of their causes.
In total eclipses of the sun a luminous ring is seen round the moon, which many astronomers take to be the atmosphere of the moon, illuminated by the sun.
A total eclipse of the sun is seen only in a narrow tract of the earth, over which the shadow of the moon passes; in other places it appears partial, or not at all.

An eclipse is an astronomical event in which an astronomical object is hidden for a time, either because it passes into the shadow of another body or because another body passes between it and the viewer.
A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth. A lunar eclipse occurs when Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon, and Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.
Solar eclipses can happen only at new moon and lunar eclipses only at full moon. Even then the Moon must be near a node, where its tilted orbit crosses the plane of Earth's orbit.
Eclipses repeat in cycles. The saros, a period of about 18 years and 11 days, was known to Babylonian astronomers and is still used to predict eclipses.
A total solar eclipse is seen only along a narrow path, usually no more than a few hundred kilometres wide, where the Moon's darkest shadow, the umbra, touches Earth.
During totality the Sun's corona, its faint outer atmosphere, becomes visible around the dark disk of the Moon.
During the solar eclipse of 1868, astronomers saw an unknown yellow line in the spectrum of the Sun. It was later traced to a new element, helium.
Many cultures saw eclipses as bad omens. Today their causes are well understood, and astronomers predict them to within seconds.

alignments.label: Light hidden by a body

britannica.quote: by the interposition of some opaque body

wikipedia.quote: another body passes between it and the viewer

alignments.note: The same definition in new words. Wikipedia uses shadow and viewer where the entry uses privation and interposition.

alignments.label: Solar and lunar eclipses

britannica.quote: when the moon comes between the sun and the earth

wikipedia.quote: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth

alignments.note: Both kinds are explained the same way in both texts.

britannica.quote: then only when the moon is near one of her nodes

wikipedia.quote: the Moon must be near a node

alignments.label: Eclipses foretold

britannica.quote: they may be foretold many years before they happen

wikipedia.quote: astronomers predict them to within seconds

alignments.note: True in 1797. The precision is now much greater. This is a change in degree, not in knowledge.

alignments.label: The Saros cycle

britannica.quote: a period of about 18 years and 11 days, which is called the Saros

wikipedia.quote: The saros, a period of about 18 years and 11 days

alignments.note: Same period in both texts. The Chaldeans of the entry are the Babylonian astronomers of Wikipedia.

alignments.label: Omens of calamity

wikipedia.quote: Today their causes are well understood

alignments.note: The verdict is for the quoted popular belief. The 1797 entry itself rejects it, so on this point the entry and Wikipedia agree.

alignments.label: Ring is moon's air

britannica.quote: the atmosphere of the moon, illuminated by the sun

wikipedia.quote: the Sun's corona, its faint outer atmosphere

alignments.note: The ring belongs to the sun, not the moon. The moon has almost no atmosphere. This is a change in knowledge.

alignments.label: Narrow track of totality

britannica.quote: seen only in a narrow tract of the earth

wikipedia.quote: seen only along a narrow path

alignments.note: The observation holds. Wikipedia names the shadow the umbra.

alignments.label: Helium in 1868

wikipedia.quote: It was later traced to a new element, helium

alignments.note: Eclipses became a tool for study of the sun. The 1797 entry treats them only as events to predict.
